sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: Accepted. The candidate preserves the required conjunctive ship conditions, the ship-to-dischargeDistanceRecords relationship and minimum count, record-level ownership for both distance properties, the >=12 nautical-mile MI_N bound, and the MI_N unit without inventing a minimum for the ice-concentration-area distance. It also preserves the prior repairs and avoids an unconditional nearby-ice property.

sheets.name: ITERATIONS
rows: Add sh:minCount 1 to the nltl:hasDischargeDistanceRecord property shape on the ship. As written, the sh:node constraint is vacuously satisfied when no discharge-distance record exists, allowing the required recording of both discharge distances to be omitted. Keep the record-level constraints and their current owners and units unchanged.

The prior sh:minCount 1 instruction for nltl:hasDischargeDistanceRecord is satisfied and must remain. Repair the semantics: do not use an sh:or branch with residueNotRecoverableByCommonMethods=false, because the requirement applies only when that value is true and the false branch creates an accidental pass. Require all stated ship conditions conjunctively. Apply the nearest-distance shape to the record's nltl:distanceToNearestLandIceShelfOrFastIce value; currently the generic QuantityValueShape omits the required >=12 nautical-mile threshold and unit. Ensure both record distance properties retain their declared dischargeDistanceRecords owner, with the nearest distance constrained by sh:minInclusive 12 and MI_N, and the ice-concentration-area distance represented without inventing a numerical minimum while enforcing its declared unit. Do not make the nearby-ice condition an unconditional ship-level pass requirement unless it is explicitly the intended direct encoding; it should support the applicable discharge-distance record condition rather than replace that relationship.

Preserve the satisfied sh:minCount 1 on nltl:hasDischargeDistanceRecord, the conjunctive ship conditions, record-level ownership, MI_N units, and the >=12 nautical-mile bound. Remove the unconditional ship-level nltl:nearbyIceConcentration requirement: it creates an extra mandatory pass condition and does not encode the applicable discharge-distance record relation. Retain the record-level nltl:distanceToAreaWithIceConcentrationGreaterThanOneTenth presence and MI_N unit without inventing a numerical minimum, and ensure the graph represents that distance as the applicable record's distance from an area exceeding 1/10 rather than as an unrelated nearby-ice value.

Accepted. The candidate preserves the required conjunctive ship conditions, the ship-to-dischargeDistanceRecords relationship and minimum count, record-level ownership for both distance properties, the >=12 nautical-mile MI_N bound, and the MI_N unit without inventing a minimum for the ice-concentration-area distance. It also preserves the prior repairs and avoids an unconditional nearby-ice property.
